questions.question: What is the difference between salt water and fresh water? Why is fresh water precious?
questions.expected_answer: Salt water has a lot of salt dissolved in it and is found in the oceans and seas; people cannot drink it or use it for crops. Fresh water has very little salt and can be used by people, animals and plants. Fresh water is precious because only about 3 out of every 100 litres of the earth's water is fresh, and most of that is frozen or underground.

questions.question: Name and explain the four main steps of the water cycle.
questions.expected_answer: Evaporation: the sun heats water and it rises as water vapour. Condensation: the vapour cools and turns into tiny drops that form clouds. Precipitation: the drops join, become heavy and fall as rain, hail or snow. Collection: water runs into rivers, lakes, dams and underground, and rivers flow back to the sea.

questions.question: Explain how Mrs Govender's experiment made fresh water from salty water.
questions.expected_answer: The sun warmed the salty water, and fresh water vapour rose while the salt stayed behind (evaporation). The vapour touched the cool plastic wrap and turned into drops (condensation). The drops ran down to the lowest point under the stone and dripped into the cup (precipitation and collection), so the water in the cup was fresh.
